Four landscapes, one park

The park climbs more than 5,000 feet in eleven miles, so you can paddle the lake in the morning and be standing in snow by lunch. Here's what you pass on the way up.

  1. 8,560 ft

    Echo Pass

    Snow most of the year, and a warming hut that's staffed all summer. The view from the top is the one on the postcards. On the way up, stop at Echo Point and give it a yell. Four echoes is normal.

  2. 6,230 ft

    Halloran Meadows

    Wildflowers peak in July. Elk graze here most evenings, so bring binoculars and keep your distance. It's also the only spot in the park where you can see the lake and the pass at the same time.

  3. 4,270 ft

    Cathedral Stand

    Old-growth cedar and Douglas fir, some of it more than 600 years old. The boardwalk loop is flat and wheelchair accessible. Please stay on it, because the roots are shallower than they look.

  4. 3,540 ft

    Echo Lake

    Eleven miles long and cold enough to make you yelp. On calm mornings it's a mirror. Canoes and kayaks rent by the hour at the lodge dock, life jackets included.
